answer: Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 112 bonds yet holds one position, and the pigment report publishes the merged exposure. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, since the willow funding graph is rebuilt from the ledge history every epoch. Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 112 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
